# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 10 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** Blessed Discipline — The Righteous and the Willful Sinner

---

**10:1** Blessed is the man whom the LORD calls to mind with reproving,
and whom he restrains from the way of evil with a scourge,

**10:2** to cleanse [him] from sin that it may not multiply,
that the LORD may humble the soul before he smites [it];

**10:3** he heals the righteous man who is disciplined in humility,
and restores his soul to the understanding of the fear of God forever.

**10:4** But the sinner who stumbles through all his days
and who does evil voluntarily — he is handed over;

**10:5** the LORD leaves him alone that he may come to himself,
for his way on earth is evil.

**10:6** He does not want the transgressor to prosper;
he prepares [his] ruin according to the evil of his way.

**10:7** He who does these things is like a man whom God has forsaken;
but the righteous man is the LORD's own beloved.

**10:8** And so, O LORD, he whom thou lovest will not stumble;
thou wilt discipline him [and not abandon him], that he may turn [to thee].

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). Hyphenated compounds preserve construct chains. Bracketed words [thus] are implied by grammar but absent from the surface text.*
